final_answer:
Let \(G\) be viewed as the Gram matrix of six unit vectors, and let
\[
A_\varepsilon
\]
be the signed adjacency matrix of the 6-cycle:
\[
(A_\varepsilon)_{i,i+1}=(A_\varepsilon)_{i+1,i}=\varepsilon_i.
\]

First note the sign pattern only matters through
\[
\sigma=\prod_{i=1}^6 \varepsilon_i.
\]
Indeed, replacing \(G\) by \(SGS\), where \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\dots,s_6)\) with \(s_i=\pm1\), preserves positive semidefiniteness, diagonal entries, and determinant, while changing edge signs by
\[
\varepsilon_i\mapsto s_i s_{i+1}\varepsilon_i.
\]
All sign patterns with the same product are equivalent by such a switching. Hence \(D_+\) and \(D_-\) are well-defined.

Now maximize \(\log\det G\). Since the feasible set contains positive definite matrices and boundary matrices have determinant \(0\), the maximizer is positive definite. At the maximizer, variations in the unspecified entries give
\[
(G^{-1})_{ij}=0
\]
for every non-edge \(ij\) of the cycle. By the signed cyclic symmetry, the inverse has the form
\[
G^{-1}=a(I+tA_\varepsilon)
\]
for some \(a>0\). Therefore
\[
G=\frac1a(I+tA_\varepsilon)^{-1}.
\]

Let
\[
M=(I+tA_\varepsilon)^{-1}.
\]
By symmetry, write \(M_{ii}=x\) and \(\varepsilon_i M_{i,i+1}=y\). The condition \(G_{ii}=1\) gives \(a=x\), while \(G_{i,i+1}=\varepsilon_i/2\) gives \(y/x=1/2\). From
\[
(I+tA_\varepsilon)M=I
\]
on a diagonal entry,
\[
x+2ty=1.
\]
Using \(y=x/2\), we get
\[
x(1+t)=1,\qquad x=\frac1{1+t}.
\]

Thus
\[
D_\sigma=\det G=\frac{(1+t)^6}{\det(I+tA_\varepsilon)}.
\]

The eigenvalues of \(A_\varepsilon\) depend only on \(\sigma\).

For \(\sigma=+1\), they are
\[
2,1,1,-1,-1,-2,
\]
so
\[
\det(I+tA_\varepsilon)=(1-4t^2)(1-t^2)^2.
\]
The condition
\[
\frac16\sum_\lambda \frac1{1+t\lambda}=\frac1{1+t}
\]
gives
\[
t=\frac{1-\sqrt{17}}8.
\]
Hence
\[
D_+=\frac{(1+t)^6}{(1-4t^2)(1-t^2)^2}
=\frac{85\sqrt{17}-349}{8}.
\]

For \(\sigma=-1\), the eigenvalues are
\[
\sqrt3,\sqrt3,0,0,-\sqrt3,-\sqrt3,
\]
so
\[
\det(I+tA_\varepsilon)=(1-3t^2)^2.
\]
The same diagonal condition gives
\[
t=1-\sqrt2.
\]
Therefore
\[
D_-=\frac{(1+t)^6}{(1-3t^2)^2}
=3-2\sqrt2.
\]

So the exact ordered pair is
\[
\boxed{\left(D_+,D_-\right)=\left(\frac{85\sqrt{17}-349}{8},\;3-2\sqrt2\right)}.
\]
